q: The first law of thermodynamics is expressed as
why: First law: heat supplied dQ = increase in internal energy dU + work done by system dW

q: In an isothermal process for an ideal gas, the quantity that remains constant is
o: internal energy only for real gas
why: Isothermal means constant temperature, so PV = nRT = constant

q: In an adiabatic process, no heat is exchanged, so the relation between internal energy and work done is
why: Adiabatic: dQ = 0, so first law gives dU = -dW

q: In a P-V diagram, the work done by a gas during an expansion equals
o: the area under the curve between initial and final volume
why: W = integral of P dV, which equals the area under the P-V curve
